display.title: Two Stories for Yud Shevat: A Letter from the Frierdiker Rebbe and the Missing Pushka
display.summary_short: Seven reasons we can trust only Hashem completely, then two true stories: a letter from the Frierdiker Rebbe that saved a life, and the Rebbe's answer about a missing pushka.
display.summary_long: Learning from this year's chapter of Basi LeGani that Hashem is everywhere, from the highest to the lowest, the storyteller explains bitachon with the seven conditions taught by Rabbeinu Bachya: to rely on someone he must love us, know our needs and not be lazy, be able to help, know what is truly good for us, have always helped, be the only one who can help, and help even when we do not deserve it. Only Hashem has all seven. Two true stories follow. The storyteller's grandparents, who spread Yiddishkeit in Pennsylvania, received a letter from the Frierdiker Rebbe telling the grandfather to be home two hours before Shabbos; the first Friday he did so, a terrible storm struck his workplace. Then the storyteller himself was chased through Flatbush by a menacing driver; when he wrote to the Rebbe, the answer told him to keep a Tehillim, Tanya and siddur in his car, with only the pushka outside the parentheses. Checking the car, he found the pushka was missing. He closes by encouraging everyone to prepare for Yud Shevat and strengthen their connection to the Rebbe.
display.lesson: Trust Hashem completely, and strengthen your connection to the Rebbe by following his instructions.
